title: Adapting DiffusionGemma PR for SYCL GPU

content.text:
this machine uses sycl instead of cuda. i want you to take https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24423 and adapt it for sycl. if i am not mistaken we should then see high gpu utilization  around 90 percent on this machine during inference. 
   when testing do not run inference until the end, only run a few passes around 5 out of the around 48 due to time constraints. use a bew wirking durectory and you might hit oom so ajust compiler jobs accordingly, you can use around 22 on this machine

macro(detect_and_find_package package_name)
    set(test_source "
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION ${CMAKE_VERSION})
    project(check_package LANGUAGES CXX)
    find_package(${package_name} QUIET)
    ")

    set(test_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/check_package_${package_name}")
    file(WRITE "${test_dir}/CMakeLists.txt" "${test_source}")

    set(cmake_args "")
    if(CMAKE_GENERATOR)
        list(APPEND cmake_args "-G" "${CMAKE_GENERATOR}")
    endif()
    if(CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM)
        list(APPEND cmake_args "-A" "${CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM}")
    endif()
    if(CMAKE_GENERATOR_TOOLSET)
        list(APPEND cmake_args "-T" "${CMAKE_GENERATOR_TOOLSET}")
    endif()
    if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER)
        list(APPEND cmake_args "-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}")
    endif()

    execute_process(
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} ${cmake_args} .
        WORKING_DIRECTORY "${test_dir}"
        RESULT_VARIABLE result
        OUTPUT_QUIET
        ERROR_QUIET
    )

    if(result EQUAL 0)
        find_package(${package_name} ${ARGN})
    else()
        message(WARNING "Detection of ${package_name} failed. The package might be broken or incompatible.")
        set(${package_name}_FOUND FALSE)
    endif()
endmacro()

macro(detect_and_find_package package_name)
    set(test_source "
    cmake_minimum_required(VERSION ${CMAKE_VERSION})
    project(check_package LANGUAGES CXX)
    find_package(${package_name} QUIET)
    ")

    set(test_dir "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/check_package_${package_name}")
    file(WRITE "${test_dir}/CMakeLists.txt" "${test_source}")

    set(cmake_args "")
    if(CMAKE_GENERATOR)
        list(APPEND cmake_args "-G" "${CMAKE_GENERATOR}")
    endif()
    if(CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM)

        list(APPEND cmake_args "-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}")
    endif()

    execute_process(
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} ${cmake_args} .
        WORKING_DIRECTORY "${test_dir}"
        RESULT_VARIABLE result
        OUTPUT_QUIET
        ERROR_QUIET
    )

    if(result EQUAL 0)
        find_package(${package_name} ${ARGN})
    else()
        message(WARNING "Detection of ${package_name} failed. The package might be broken or incompatible.")

arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash
# GPU busy% sampler: sums per-fd drm-engine counters from /proc/<pid>/fdinfo (Xe/i915 expose
# cumulative per-engine busy time there - same source nvtop uses) and reports busy/period.
# Usage: gpu_busy.sh <pid> <interval_s> [seconds]
pid=$1
interval=${2:-1}
seconds=${3:-0}

read_engines() {
    local sum=0
    for f in /proc/$pid/fdinfo/*; do
        [ -r "$f" ] || continue
        # drm-engine-*: <ns>; some kernels report <ms> - Xe reports ns per docs (values ~1e9+ scale)
        while read -r _ v _; do
            sum=$((sum + v))
        done < <(grep -E '^drm-engine-' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
    done
    echo $sum
}

prev=$(read_engines)
t0=$(date +%s.%N)
elapsed=0
while true; do
    sleep "$interval"
    [ -r "/proc/$pid/stat" ] || { echo "process exited"; break; }
    now=$(read_engines)
    t1=$(date +%s.%N)
    d_ns=$((now - prev))
    d_t=$(echo "$t1 $t0" | awk '{printf "%.3f", $2 - $1}')
    pct=$(echo "$d_ns $d_t" | awk '{ if ($2 > 0) printf "%.1f", 100.0 * $1 / ($2 * 1e9); else print "0.0" }')
    freq=$(cat /sys/class/drm/card1/gt_act_freq_mhz 2>/dev/null)
    echo "t=${d_t}s gpu_busy=${pct}% gt_act_freq=${freq}MHz"
    prev=$now
    t0=$t1
    elapsed=$(echo "$elapsed $interval" | awk '{print $1 + $2}')
    if [ "$seconds" -gt 0 ] && awk "BEGIN{exit !($elapsed >= $seconds)}"; then break; fi
done

#!/bin/bash
# Run2: same5-step diffusion smoke test, but sample per-fd per-engine drm busy counters and
# report render-engine (rcs) busy%% for the diffusion-step window only (from the first
# "diffusion step:" log line to process exit).
cd /home/asdf/Downloads/sycl-work/llama-sycl || exit 1
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh >/dev/null 2>&1

MODEL=$HOME/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--unsloth--diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-GGUF/snapshots/f4183a2c7a354128d02545752303c4354d165bf0/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf
BIN=./build/bin/llama-diffusion-cli

"$BIN" -m "$MODEL" -ngl 99 -p "Write a short haiku about the ocean." -n 256 --diffusion-eb-max-steps 5 > run2.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "PID=$PID"

declare -A prev
active=0
rcs_sum=0; rcs_n=0; rcs_max=0
all_sum=0

flush_samples() { :; }

while true; do
    state=$(awk '{print $3}' /proc/$PID/stat 2>/dev/null)
    [ -z "$state" ] && break
    [ "$state" = "Z" ] && break
    sleep 1
    if [ "$active" = 0 ] && grep -q "diffusion step:" run2.log 2>/dev/null; then
        active=1
        echo "=== diffusion phase starts ==="
    fi
    t=$(date +%s%N)
    declare -A cur=()
    for f in /proc/$PID/fdinfo/*; do
        [ -r "$f" ] || continue
        fd=$(basename "$f")
        while read -r k v; do
            cur["$fd:$k"]=$v
        done < <(grep -E '^drm-engine-' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
    done
    rcs_max_tick=0; all_tick=0
    for key in "${!cur[@]}"; do
        p=${prev[$key]:-0}
        d=$(( cur[$key] - p ))
        [ "$d" -lt 0 ] && d=0
        all_tick=$(( all_tick + d ))
        if [[ "$key" == *drm-engine-rcs ]]; then
            [ "$d" -gt "$rcs_max_tick" ] && rcs_max_tick=$d
        fi
    done
    prev=()
    for key in "${!cur[@]}"; do prev[$key]=${cur[$key]}; done
    if [ -n "$last_t" ]; then
        dt_ns=$(( t - last_t ))
        if [ "$dt_ns" -gt 0 ] && [ "$active" = 1 ]; then
            rcs_pct=$(( rcs_max_tick * 100 / dt_ns ))
            all_pct=$(( all_tick * 100 / dt_ns ))
            freq=$(cat /sys/class/drm/card1/gt_act_freq_mhz 2>/dev/null)
            echo "rcs_busy=${rcs_pct}% all_engines_sum=${all_pct}% gt_act_freq=${freq}MHz"
            rcs_sum=$(( rcs_sum + rcs_pct )); rcs_n=$(( rcs_n + 1 ))
            [ "$rcs_pct" -gt "$rcs_max" ] && rcs_max=$rcs_pct
            all_sum=$(( all_sum + all_pct ))
        fi
    fi
    last_t=$t
    unset cur
done
wait $PID; rc=$?
echo "EXIT_CODE=$rc"
if [ "$rcs_n" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "STEP_PHASE_RCS_BUSY_AVG=$(( rcs_sum / rcs_n ))% MAX=${rcs_max}% ALL_ENGINES_AVG=$(( all_sum / rcs_n ))% SAMPLES=$rcs_n"
fi
echo "=== run2.log tail ==="
tail -12 run2.log

sources.title: Forks
sources.snippet:
When you view a forked repository on GitHub, the upstream repository is indicated below the name of the fork.
You can fork any public repository:
* To your personal account
* To an organization where you have permission to create repositories
If you have access to a private repository and the owner permits forking, you can fork the repository:
* To your personal account
* To an organization on GitHub Team where you have permission to create repositories
You cannot fork a private repository to an organization using GitHub Free. For more information about GitHub Team and GitHub Free, see GitHub's plans.
Repository, organization, and enterprise policies can limit whether repositories can be forked and where forks can be created.
For private repositories, access to forks also depends on repository visibility, organization membership, and administrator settings.
If you're a member of an enterprise with managed users, additional restrictions apply to the repositories you can fork. See About Enterprise Managed Users in the GitHub Enterprise Cloud documentation.
A fork's visibility depends on the upstream repository. Public repository forks are public, and private repository forks are private. You cannot change the visibility of a fork by itself.
A repository network includes the upstream repository, its forks, and forks of those forks.
Repositories in the network share Git data and remain connected to the upstream repository. See Understanding connections between repositories.
Deleting a repository or changing its visibility can affect the network. If you delete a fork, code contributions from that fork can remain accessible to the repository network.
For more information, see Managing the forking policy for your organization and Managing the forking policy for your repository.
Visibility changes can separate forks into new repository networks so that existing fork owners can keep working without unexpected loss of access.
* Action | Effect on forks
* A private repository is deleted | Its private forks are also deleted.
* A public repository is deleted | An active public fork becomes the new upstream repository for the network.
* A public repository is made private | Its public forks stay public in a separate network.
* A private repository is made public | Private forks stay private but disconnect into separate private networks.
Changing a public repository to private can also affect stars, watchers, dependency graph, Dependabot alerts, and code scanning availability. Review repository visibility settings carefully before changing them.
Internal repositories support a single level of forking. You cannot fork a private fork of an internal repository. This keeps access and management simpler for repositories that are visible across an enterprise.

About permissions and visibility of forks
The permissions and visibility of forks depend on whether the upstream repository is public or private, whether it is owned by an organization, and the policies of your enterprise.
About permissions for creating forks
You can fork a private or internal repository to your personal account or to an organization on GitHub where you have permission to create repositories, provided that the settings for the repository and your enterprise policies allow forking.
Generally, you can fork any public repository to your personal account or to an organization where you have permission to create repositories.
* If you fork a private repository that belongs to a personal account, external collaborators also get access to the fork.
* If you fork a private or internal repository that belongs to an organization, teams within the organization get access to the fork, but external collaborators do not.
* You can add an external collaborator to a fork of a private repository that belongs to an organization if you are an owner of that organization or if your organization allows repository administrators to invite external collaborators.
Organizations can allow or prevent the forking of any private repositories owned by the organization, and enterprises can enforce policies to specify where members can create forks of private or internal repositories. Policies control the options available to the enterprise's organizations.

All repositories belong to a repository network.
If you delete a repository or change the repository's visibility settings, you will affect the repository's forks. For more information, see What happens to forks when a repository is deleted or changes visibility?
If you delete a fork, any code contributions of that fork will still be accessible to the repository network.
Public forks do not inherit the permissions structure of the upstream repository.
When you fork a public repository to your personal account, you can allow repository maintainers to push to your pull request branch. This includes giving them permission to make commits or delete the branch.

How can I fork a public repository, but make my fork private? I do have the subscription to support private repositories.
First, duplicate the repo as others said (details here ):
Create a new repo (let's call it private-repo ) via the Github UI . Then:
git clone --bare https://github.com/exampleuser/public-repo.git
cd public-repo.git
git push --mirror https://github.com/yourname/private-repo.git
cd ..
rm -rf public-repo.git
Clone the private repo so you can work on it:
git clone https://github.com/yourname/private-repo.git
cd private-repo
make some changes
git commit
git push origin master
To pull new hotness from the public repo:
cd private-repo
git remote add public https://github.com/exampleuser/public-repo.git
git pull public master # Creates a merge commit
git push origin master
Awesome, your private repo now has the latest code from the public repo plus your changes.
Finally, to create a pull request private repo -> public repo:
Use the GitHub UI to create a fork of the public repo (the small "Fork" button at the top right of the public repo page). Then:
git clone https://github.com/yourname/the-fork.git
cd the-fork
git remote add private_repo_yourname https://github.com/yourname/private-repo.git
git checkout -b pull_request_yourname
git pull private_repo_yourname master
git push origin pull_request_yourname
Now you can create a pull request via the Github UI for public-repo, as described here .
Set the push location to your mirror
Simply fork the repository and then do
gh repo edit --visibility private <link to your fork>
Your repo will be shortly unavailable because it's "moving to another place", probably for security because normally

2. Leave fork network and confirm

#!/bin/bash
# Run4: same5-step test; per-engine breakdown of drm fdinfo busy counters (max over fds of
# per-engine busy%%), to attribute GPU utilization to the correct engine.
cd /home/asdf/Downloads/sycl-work/llama-sycl || exit 1
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh >/dev/null 2>&1

MODEL=$HOME/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--unsloth--diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-GGUF/snapshots/f4183a2c7a354128d02545752303c4354d165bf0/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf
BIN=./build/bin/llama-diffusion-cli

"$BIN" -m "$MODEL" -ngl 99 -p "Write a short haiku about the ocean." -n 256 --diffusion-eb-max-steps 5 > run4.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "PID=$PID"

declare -A prev
active=0
declare -A agg_max agg_sum agg_n
all_sum=0; all_n=0

while true; do
    state=$(awk '{print $3}' /proc/$PID/stat 2>/dev/null)
    [ -z "$state" ] && break
    [ "$state" = "Z" ] && break
    sleep 1
    if [ "$active" = 0 ] && grep -q "diffusion step:" run4.log 2>/dev/null; then
        active=1
        echo "=== diffusion phase ==="
    fi
    t=$(date +%s%N)
    declare -A cur=()
    nfd=0
    for f in /proc/$PID/fdinfo/*; do
        [ -r "$f" ] || continue
        got=$(grep -E '^drm-engine-' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
        [ -n "$got" ] || continue
        nfd=$((nfd + 1))
        fd=$(basename "$f")
        while read -r k v _u; do
            cur["$fd:$k"]=$v
        done <<< "$got"
    done
    # per-engine max single-fd delta
    declare -A tick_max
    all_tick=0
    for key in "${!cur[@]}"; do
        p=${prev[$key]:-0}
        d=$(( cur[$key] - p ))
        [ "$d" -lt 0 ] && d=0
        all_tick=$(( all_tick + d ))
        eng=${key#*:}
        m=${tick_max[$eng]:-0}
        [ "$d" -gt "$m" ] && tick_max[$eng]=$d
    done
    prev=()
    for key in "${!cur[@]}"; do prev[$key]=${cur[$key]}; done
    if [ -n "$last_t" ] && [ "$active" = 1 ]; then
        dt_ns=$(( t - last_t ))
        if [ "$dt_ns" -gt 0 ]; then
            line="nfd=$nfd"
            for eng in "${!tick_max[@]}"; do
                pct=$(( tick_max[$eng] * 100 / dt_ns ))
                short=${eng#drm-engine-}
                line="$line $short=${pct}%"
                a=${agg_max[$eng]:-0}; [ "$pct" -gt "$a" ] && agg_max[$eng]=$pct
                agg_sum[$eng]=$(( ${agg_sum[$eng]:-0} + pct ))
                agg_n[$eng]=$(( ${agg_n[$eng]:-0} + 1 ))
            done
            apct=$(( all_tick * 100 / dt_ns ))
            line="$line sum=${apct}%"
            all_sum=$(( all_sum + apct )); all_n=$(( all_n + 1 ))
            echo "$line"
        fi
    fi
    last_t=$t
    unset cur tick_max
done
wait $PID; rc=$?
echo "EXIT_CODE=$rc"
for eng in "${!agg_sum[@]}"; do
    echo "ENGINE ${eng#drm-engine-}: avg=$(( agg_sum[$eng] / agg_n[$eng] ))% max=${agg_max[$eng]}% samples=${agg_n[$eng]}"
done
[ "$all_n" -gt 0 ] && echo "SUM_ALL_ENGINES: avg=$(( all_sum / all_n ))% samples=$all_n"
echo "=== run4.log tail ==="
grep -E "sample_reduce|diffusion step|total time|throughput" run4.log | tail -8
tail -4 run4.log

Done. Summary of what happened:

## Port (reusing the PR's CUDA work, as you said)
The PR's only CUDA-specific piece is the Stage-1 dense device sampler (`ggml-cuda/diffusion-sampling.cu`) plus a proc-address hook. I ported it nearly1:1 into the SYCL backend in a fresh working dir `~/Downloads/sycl-work/llama-sycl` (branch `diffusion-gemma-sycl` on PR head `dd7f73b19`):

- **New** `ggml/src/ggml-sycl/diffusion-sampling.{hpp,cpp}` — same kernel logic: one work-group (256) per canvas position, local-memory max→argmax + Z/entropy reductions, slice-parallel multinomial draw; same grow-only per-device scratch, registered as `ggml_backend_sycl_diffusion_sample` in `ggml_backend_sycl_reg_get_proc_address` (`CMakeLists.txt` needs no edit — it globs `*.cpp`).
- `src/models/diffusion-gemma.cpp` — `llama_diffusion_device_sample` now probes every reg+proc pair (CUDA/ROCm/MUSA + **SYCL**) instead of only the CUDA family.
- Cosmetic: CUDA-specific log/doc strings in `diffusion-cli.cpp`/`llama.h` generalized to "GPU". `sc_dev`/KV-store allocation was already backend-generic (`dev_layer(0)` buft), so no other change was needed.

## Build & test
- `icpx` (oneAPI 2026.1, `icx`/`icpx` explicit — the first build silently picked system g++ and failed on `-fsycl`), `-j22`, no OOM, ~8.6 min, `llama-diffusion-cli` linked.
- Model: the already-cached `diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf` (16 GB). Ran4 smoke runs, each capped at **5 of the default 48** denoising steps (`--diffusion-eb-max-steps 5`), canvas_length=256, `-n 256` → 1 block. EXIT 0 every time, haiku output produced; warm step time ~17–19 s.
- Log proves the port is live: `gpu_sampling=on sample_reduce=on` and **no** "on-device sampling unsupported; using host sampling" warning — i.e. `llama_diffusion_device_sample` resolved the SYCL sampler and the per-step 268 MB logits D2H + host reductions stayed off the path.

## GPU utilization (~90% expectation)
Measured via i915 per-client `drm-engine-*` fdinfo counters during the step window:
- `compute` + `copy` engines accumulate **continuously** through each denoise step; ~46/58 one-second ticks busy (**~80% of step wall time**), idle ticks only at step/block transitions.
- During busy ticks each engine reads ~90–130% of wall (i915's counter can overcount slightly), i.e. engines saturated in compute bursts; `gt_act_freq` sits at 250–600 of 2250 MHz — the workload is memory-bound on shared LPDDR, so utilization is high but clocks throttle.
- So: high utilization as expected, with ~20% of the step window lost to transition overhead, not to host sampling.

## Published
GitHub forbids private forks of public repos (API 422 "Public forks can't be made private"), so:
- **Private** standalone repo: https://github.com/alosslessdev/llama.cpp-sycl-diffusion, branch `diffusion-gemma-sycl` @ `ce61e7e5a` (PR head + one port commit) — verified `private: true`.
- The same branch also landed on your existing **public** fork `alosslessdev/llama.cpp` (pushed before the privacy constraint surfaced). Say the word if you want me to delete that public branch.

Caveat: I did not run the full 48-step denoise per your instruction; scratch scripts/logs were removed, and disk stayed at 2.1 GB free throughout (the 99%-full root fs is the one thing worth cleaning on this machine).

#!/bin/bash
# Full run: all denoising steps (default48, entropy-bound early exit possible). Same per-engine
# busy sampling as the instrumented smoke tests, over the whole run.
cd /home/asdf/Downloads/sycl-work/llama-sycl || exit 1
source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh >/dev/null 2>&1

MODEL=$HOME/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--unsloth--diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-GGUF/snapshots/f4183a2c7a354128d02545752303c4354d165bf0/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-Q4_K_M.gguf
BIN=./build/bin/llama-diffusion-cli

"$BIN" -m "$MODEL" -ngl 99 -p "Write a short haiku about the ocean." -n 256 > run_full.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "PID=$PID start=$(date +%T)"

declare -A prev
active=0
declare -A agg_sum agg_n
all_sum=0; all_n=0; busy_n=0

while true; do
    state=$(awk '{print $3}' /proc/$PID/stat 2>/dev/null)
    [ -z "$state" ] && break
    [ "$state" = "Z" ] && break
    sleep 1
    if [ "$active" = 0 ] && grep -q "diffusion step:" run_full.log 2>/dev/null; then
        active=1
        echo "=== diffusion phase starts $(date +%T) ==="
    fi
    t=$(date +%s%N)
    declare -A cur=()
    for f in /proc/$PID/fdinfo/*; do
        [ -r "$f" ] || continue
        got=$(grep -E '^drm-engine-(copy|compute|render|video|video-enhance):' "$f" 2>/dev/null)
        [ -n "$got" ] || continue
        fd=$(basename "$f")
        while read -r k v _u; do
            [ -n "$v" ] || continue
            cur["$fd:$k"]=$v
        done <<< "$got"
    done
    declare -A tick_max=()
    all_tick=0
    for key in "${!cur[@]}"; do
        p=${prev[$key]:-0}
        d=$(( cur[$key] - p ))
        [ "$d" -lt 0 ] && d=0
        all_tick=$(( all_tick + d ))
        eng=${key#*:}
        m=${tick_max[$eng]:-0}
        [ "$d" -gt "$m" ] && tick_max[$eng]=$d
    done
    prev=()
    for key in "${!cur[@]}"; do prev[$key]=${cur[$key]}; done
    if [ -n "$last_t" ] && [ "$active" = 1 ]; then
        dt_ns=$(( t - last_t ))
        if [ "$dt_ns" -gt 0 ]; then
            apct=$(( all_tick * 100 / dt_ns ))
            all_sum=$(( all_sum + apct )); all_n=$(( all_n + 1 ))
            [ "$apct" -gt 0 ] && busy_n=$(( busy_n + 1 ))
            for eng in "${!tick_max[@]}"; do
                pct=$(( tick_max[$eng] * 100 / dt_ns ))
                agg_sum[$eng]=$(( ${agg_sum[$eng]:-0} + pct ))
                agg_n[$eng]=$(( ${agg_n[$eng]:-0} + 1 ))
            done
            # progress line every30s
            if [ $(( all_n % 30 )) -eq 0 ]; then
                last_step=$(grep -o "diffusion step: [0-9]*/[0-9]*" run_full.log | tail -1)
                freq=$(cat /sys/class/drm/card1/gt_act_freq_mhz 2>/dev/null)
                echo "$(date +%T) samples=$all_n busy_ticks=$busy_n last=[$last_step] gt_freq=${freq}MHz"
            fi
        fi
    fi
    last_t=$t
    unset cur tick_max
done
wait $PID; rc=$?
echo "EXIT_CODE=$rc end=$(date +%T)"
for eng in "${!agg_sum[@]}"; do
    echo "ENGINE ${eng#drm-engine-}: avg=$(( agg_sum[$eng] / agg_n[$eng] ))% samples=${agg_n[$eng]}"
done
[ "$all_n" -gt 0 ] && echo "PHASE: samples=$all_n busy_ticks=$busy_n busy_coverage=$(( busy_n * 100 / all_n ))% avg_all_engines=$(( all_sum / all_n ))%"
echo "=== run_full.log key lines ==="
grep -E "max_steps|diffusion step|total time|throughput" run_full.log | tail -12
echo "=== output ==="
tail -15 run_full.log

Right now, while the run is live, easiest unprivileged options (this machine has no passwordless sudo and `perf_event_paranoid=4`, so `intel_gpu_top` won't work for me — but it will for you in a terminal where you can enter your password):

**1. Per-client engine busy (what I used) — works unprivileged:**

```bash
# find the inference process
pid=$(pgrep -f llama-diffusion-cli)

# sample engine busy deltas for ~5s and print busy%
f=/proc/$pid/fdinfo/3          # fd3 is the renderD128 handle that carries the work
a=$(grep -E '^drm-engine-(copy|compute)' $f | awk '{s+=$2} END{print s}')
sleep 5
b=$(grep -E '^drm-engine-(copy|compute)' $f | awk '{s+=$2} END{print s}')
echo "busy ~$(( (b-a)/50000000 ))% (sum of copy+compute engines; divide by2 for rough per-engine)"
```

Values are cumulative nanoseconds; I logged 1-second samples of these into a loop — during the denoise steps it sat at engines-busy essentially every tick, dropping to0 only between steps.

**2. Clock proxy (instant, dead simple):**

```bash
watch -n1 cat /sys/class/drm/card1/gt_act_freq_mhz   # max is2250
```
It fluctuates250–600 MHz under this workload: the iGPU is busy but memory-bandwidth-bound, so it doesn't boost — low clocks alone don't mean idle.

**3. The proper tool (needs your password):**

```bash
sudo apt install intel-gpu-tools
sudo intel_gpu_top        # shows Engine %/Render/Blitter/Video per engine, like nvidia-smi
```
On Meteor Lake it will show the `RCS/CCS` (compute) and `BCS` (copy) rows busy at high % during each step — this is the tool whose numbers I couldn't run, and it reports clean per-engine percentages without the fdinfo overcount caveat (~×1.3 in my measurements).

# omp-archive

Export the **entire** history of an omp session as one zip: the main transcript,
every subagent session (recursively, verbatim), all untruncated tool /
background-job output, live background-job state, and a standalone HTML viewer.

`/export` embeds subagent *entries* in a viewer HTML and `/dump` covers the live
main conversation. Neither ships a subagent's own transcript file, its sibling
tool-output logs, or background-job state. This plugin archives all of it.

## Install

```bash
# local checkout / development (symlinked, edits are live)
omp plugin link /home/asdf/projects/omp-archive

# git
omp plugin install github:<user>/omp-archive

# marketplace (this repo ships .omp-plugin/marketplace.json)
/marketplace add <user>/omp-archive
/marketplace install archive@omp-archive

# one-off
omp --extension /home/asdf/projects/omp-archive
```

## Usage

```
/archive                      # -> ./omp-archive-<session>.zip
/archive /tmp/session.zip
/archive --no-artifacts       # skip the artifact/log tree (smaller zip)
/archive --no-viewer          # skip viewer.html
```

The same operation is exposed as the `export_session_archive` tool so the agent
can archive a session on request.

## What's inside

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `manifest.json` | Index of everything below: counts, sizes, subagent list, omissions |
| `session.jsonl` | The main session transcript, byte-for-byte |
| `agents.json` | Live per-agent state captured while the session ran (model, system prompt, tools) |
| `jobs.json` | Background/async jobs: `completed` (recovered from every transcript) plus `live` (running/recent at archive time) |
| `artifacts/` | **Every** file under the session artifact directory, byte-for-byte |
| `viewer.html` | Standalone HTML viewer with all subagent sessions embedded |
| `README.md` | Human-readable index of the archive |

`artifacts/` is the complete record: each subagent's own
`<AgentId>.jsonl` (nested children under `<AgentId>/`), the
`*.bash.log` / `*.eval.log` / `*.read.log` files holding the **full,
untruncated** tool and background-job output that the transcript truncates, and
`*.jsonl.tombstone` kill markers.

## Limits

- **Background jobs.** `jobs.json` lists two sources: `completed` — every

Use top-level `import type` declarations for type-only dependencies. NEVER write `import("pkg").Type` inside source annotations.

// Bad — inline imports hide dependencies in signatures.

import type { Client } from "some-sdk";
import type { ClientOptions } from "some-sdk/config";
import type { infer as Infer } from "arktype";

function run(client: Client, input: Infer<Schema>): Promise<Output>;

- Generated files whose generator owns import management.
